question: On New Year's Eve, Uber's surge pricing in New York broke for 26 minutes. What happened to people trying to get a ride?
options: More got rides, at normal fares
answer: Most requests went unfilled. With fares stuck at normal levels, requests jumped while no extra drivers were drawn onto the roads, so only about a quarter of requests were completed and waiting times soared. When surge pricing was working, almost every request found a car. A capped fare meant, for most, no ride at all.
move: Before cheering a capped price, ask who will now go without.
ask: When something I want is cheap but always sold out, what am I paying instead?
trap: Expecting normal fares to help riders, since nobody paid extra.
source: Hall, Kendrick and Nosko, Uber case study, 2015
reference: Hall, Kendrick & Nosko, The Effects of Uber's Surge Pricing: A Case Study, University of Chicago Booth School of Business, 2015
